newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open moderately higher on Thursday, but traders would remain hesitant ahead of tomorrow's U.S. unemployment data.
Stocks could be boosted by short-covering and an expected strengthening of the technology sector, which has been hurt by recent profit warnings and the fears that more were coming.
A stronger-than-expected rise in jobless claims for the week ended May 31 also gave some early morning strength to stock futures and inflation-wary bonds.
Claims rose to 337,000 for the week versus a revised 318,000 in the previous week and a forecast 320,000.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was trading up 2.60 points at 844.70. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 1/32 at a 6.88 percent yield.

"We should see a slight drift to the upside this morning with techs firming, but on balance, buyers will be cautious before the unemployment data," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said.
